subject: Post-call recap: SLO mapping, routing & data-residency checklist
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alicia Wang <aw@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-22T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: SLO mapping, routing & data-residency checklist

Alicia — thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our call plus the few clarifying items we said we'd follow up on. Please correct anything I get wrong.

1) Business goals / targets (what you confirmed on the call)
- Primary region: US (east) for 70% of traffic; EU for 25% (GDPR/data residency for EU customers); APAC pilot 5% (Singapore).
- Target observable SLOs: p50 <= 80ms, p95 <= 220ms for non-streaming single-turn text generation (chat-like flows).
- Streaming requirements: startup/first-byte ideally < 200ms for long streaming responses; steady-state token-rate target ~20–40 TPS per connection.
- Peak throughput & concurrency: baseline 200 rps sustained across regions, burst to 700 rps during campaign windows; expected concurrent active sessions ~600 worldwide (with per-region concurrency limits).
- Availability: 99.9% target for inference endpoints; failover to secondary region acceptable for non-sensitive traffic.

2) Residency & compliance constraints
- EU customer data must remain in EU for storage & logs; transients in-flight across regions acceptable only if encrypted and logged (you mentioned full EU residency for customer A).
- Audit evidence: you requested SOC2 + dataflow diagram and an option for VPC/private deployment for PHI-sensitive subsets.

3) Technical asks we committed to deliver by Friday:
- Fillable SLO worksheet for your workload (attached).
- Initial cost/throughput sketch for the three region+failover configuration.
- List of required artifacts for SOC2 + dataflow diagram (we'll include a redacted sample).

Next steps:
- I'll schedule a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Rishi and Diego to map traffic profiles and run a quick PoC sizing exercise (propose Tue/Thu next week).
- You (Alicia) will confirm which customer groups require strict EU residency and identify the technical contact for firewall/VPC networking (Luca?).
- We'll deliver the SLO worksheet + sketch by EOD Friday (attached).

Attachments: redwood_slo_worksheet_v1.xlsx (SLO template), acuity_prod_requirements_summary.pdf (notes from call).

Thanks — Camila

--
Camila Reyes | Account Executive | Redwood Inference

Date: 2025-08-22T17:12:00+02:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLO mapping, routing & data-residency checklist

Thanks Camila — this is accurate and helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- The p95 number you listed (220ms) is for user-facing conversational latency when using the smaller family of models (we'll evaluate quality tradeoffs). For longer, multi-turn generation we expect p95 to be higher but want to ensure first-byte/startup is low for streaming.
- EU residency: for our EU enterprise customers all prompt/response logs must be stored in EU and never replicated outside. Runtime inference can happen in US for speed only if we use a strict edge-only mode and ensure no logs leave EU; otherwise we need EU-only serving.
- APAC: we are okay with a single-region pilot in Singapore but latency target there is p95 <= 350ms.
- We will provide a spreadsheet with estimated qps per customer segment by EOD Wednesday.

Can you also include a short note on how Redwood handles automatic fallback between regions when a region is saturated? We want to avoid cross-border logging unless explicitly permitted.

--
Alicia Wang
Head of Platform Integrations | Acuity Health
aw@acuityhealth.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Alicia Wang <aw@acuityhealth.com>, Luca Bianchi <luca@acuityhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood.ai>
Date: 2025-08-23T09:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: SLO mapping, routing & data-residency checklist

Alicia / team — quick technical notes based on Camila's summary and your follow-up: 

- Throughput/concurrency: Redwood supports per-customer and per-route concurrency limits. For your numbers (200 rps baseline, bursts to 700 rps), we'd recommend a combination of dedicated capacity pools for the US/EU and a small burst pool for APAC during campaign windows. This keeps predictable p95 behavior.
- Latency guidance: p50 60–80ms is realistic on latest open model variants in a dedicated-inference setup with warm KV caches. p95 at ~200–250ms for single-turn generation is achievable with target sequence lengths (<= 256 tokens). Longer contexts increase p95 non-linearly.
- Streaming: startup time depends on cold vs warm model; with prefix caching and pre-warmed worker slots we can hit 120–200ms first-byte on typical prompts. Steady-state token throughput of 25–35 tokens/sec per stream is typical; we can scale concurrent streams horizontally.
- Multi-region routing & residency: Redwood supports policy-based routing: route-by-region, route-by-tenant, or route-by-data-residency flag. For strict EU residency we can provision EU-only endpoints (no cross-border replication of logs). For failover, we support optional blocked-fallback (fail requests instead of routing cross-region) or permissive-fallback (route to fallback region). Logging controls: logs can be restricted to region and you can enable anonymization/redaction for cross-border cases.
- Operational ask: to size a PoC we need 48 hours of representative traffic (qps + typical prompt lengths) and one config file with per-route expected concurrency.

I'll join the tech deep-dive. Camila — let's coordinate schedules.

--
Rishi Malhotra | Senior Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Alicia / Luca — thanks for the clarifications, this is great. Quick actionable plan and dates: 

1) Technical deep-dive (60m) — propose Tue 2025-08-26 10:00 PST / 19:00 CET (Rishi + Diego + Camila). Please confirm or propose alternate.
2) PoC sizing: share 48 hours of representative traffic dump (anonymized) by Friday 2025-08-29. Rishi will run a baseline sizing and provide recommended dedicated pool configurations.
3) Residency artifacts: I'll attach a redacted dataflow and SOC2 checklist in a follow-up email; please flag any additional items.
4) Fallback policy: default we propose is blocked-fallback for Eu-residency customers unless you sign off on permissive-fallback for specific non-sensitive routes. We'll include this in the SLO worksheet.

Attached: redwood_slo_worksheet_v1.xlsx (filled with our initial assumptions), acuity_prod_requirements_summary.pdf (annotated).

Next action items for Acuity: confirm tech contact for networking (Luca), confirm EU-only tenant list, and send anonymized traffic sample. For Redwood: deliver PoC sizing + cost sketch within 5 business days of receiving traffic.

Looking forward — Camila
